2. The petitioner instituted the above suit for permanent injunction with a prayer for temporary injunction for restraining the defendant opposite party from executing any document in respect of the suit property, constructing any building or digging any earth and changing the character of the land of the 'Ka' schedule property till the disposal of the suit claiming title to the suit property through inheritance as well as by purchase. The defendant opposite parties entered appearance and filed written objection denying the material allegations made in the application for injunction and contended that 0.08 acre of land appertaining to plot No.154 described in "Ka" schedule of the plaint was purchased by the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 who are also heirs of the original owner Abdul Majid through their predecessor-in-interest Md Yusuf Ali and got exclusive possession in 0.80 acre of land of plot No. 154. The defendant No. 6 transferred the said land along with some other lands to defendant No.5 by registered Kabala dated 21-7-91 and after the purchase got exclusive possession of the said "Kha" schedule land. The defendant No.3 obtained mutation Khatian No. 422 and thereafter by registered Kabala dated 3-4-96 transferred the same to defendant No.4 who out of her nobility gifted the said land to the opposite party No.3 the Girls High School, for extension of women's education in the locality and with the help and supervision of the Facilities Department of the Government construction work of school building was going on covering plot Nos. 155, 153 and suit plot No. 154 and, in fact, the work of school building almost has been completed. He further asserted that the plaintiff petitioner never had any exclusive possession of the said "Kha" schedule land at the time of filing of the suit and only to cause harassment and inconvenience the suit has been filed. The learned trial Court vide his Order No. 12 dated 23-11-96 passed an order for maintaining status quo in respect of the suit land till the disposal of the suit, Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the trial Court the defendant opposite parties preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Noakhali, which was registered as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 53 of 1996 and on an application of the defendant opposite parties stayed the operation of the order dated 23-11-96 of the trial Court granting status quo prohibiting construction in the suit land till the disposal of the suit. Being aggrieved by the order of stay dated 30-11-96 passed by the learned District Judge, Noakhali, in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal the plaintiff petitioner preferred this revisional application and obtained the instant Rule. 

 4. Mr Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite parties, submits that the instant suit is a suit for permanent injunction with a prayer for temporary injunction and it is clear from the order, dated 23-11-96 passed by the trial Court that the plaintiff petitioner is out of possession of the suit land and the defendant opposite parties are in possession of the "Kha" schedule land and, as such, the appellate Court below had sufficient materials .before it for passing an order of stay. The learned Advocate further submits that in a suit for permanent injunction the plaintiff can only succeed if he can prove that he is in exclusive possession of the suit land but in the instant case it is crystal clear from the averments made in the plaint as well as in the injunction application that the plaintiff-petitioner is not in exclusive possession of the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case the suit land has been mutated in the name of the defendant No. 5 and thereafter the land was transferred to the defendant No.4 and this mutation Khatian coupled with the inspection report dated 20-10-96 conclusively proved that the defendant-opposite parties are in possession of the disputed land and, as such, the learned appellate Court below after admission of the appeal rightly stayed the operation of the order of status quo passed by the trial Court, In support of his contention he relies on the decisions reported in 31 DLR(AD) 319, 35 DLR 25 and AIR 1933 (Bom)118.
